subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub standardize Weekly/Monthly/All time popularity across creators, skills, and plugins with shared temporal stats, publisher aggregation, and snapshot-pinned pagination before shipping visible tabs?
rationale: Current main only has partial seven-day Trending support, while the requested cross-surface behavior needs maintainer choices for scoring, attribution, low-activity handling, and rollout/backfill semantics.

options.title: Approve shared foundation first
options.body: Define the period semantics and data model, then implement daily rollups and weekly/monthly leaderboards before adding visible browse tabs.

options.title: Keep existing Trending only
options.body: Leave the current skills/plugins Trending affordance in place and defer publisher/monthly alignment until a maintainer sponsors the broader contract.

options.title: Document before implementation
options.body: Capture the intended contract in specs and wait for a smaller implementation plan before changing backend or UI behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve shared foundation first
recommendation.body: Define the period semantics and data model, then implement daily rollups and weekly/monthly leaderboards before adding visible browse tabs.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history points to this owner around the browse and leaderboard paths that would need the cross-surface contract decision.
